messages:
kevin: Quick follow-up from the kernel RFC — we ran the small-batch chat latency tests yesterday and results are... messy.

sophie: TL;DR numbers? :eyes:

kevin: 1) Triton path best for throughput on long sequences. 2) CUTLASS kernels win single-request latency for seq<=128 in our microbench. 3) But CUTLASS regresses on dynamic kv-cache eviction patterns.

raj: Can you paste the bench commands and env?

kevin: Sure. Ran on p4d. Command: ```python bench_attention.py --model gpt-like --batch 1 --seq 64 --kv-dynamic True --iters 200``` Env: CUDA 12.2, driver 535, cudnn 9.1, triton 2.4.

maria: Interesting, the kv-dynamic flag toggles our cache invalidation workload. That could explain fragmentation.

devon: Is the CUTLASS path using our shared workspace allocator? I remember an issue where allocation/free jitter increased p99.

kevin: Yes, CUTLASS uses the per-infer temporary allocator (fast_free) — which is lockfree but doesn't compact. Triton runtime uses a pooled allocator more conservatively.

raj: So real-world chat = many short sequences with prefix reuse and lots of small allocs. That favors Triton's memory plan even if raw kernel latency is higher.

kevin: Exactly. But we can't ignore the CUTLASS latency win for certain configs. Proposal: keep both paths, add policy routing by request profile (seq_len, kv-delta, latency-SLO).

sophie: Can we do automatic sampling during warmup to pick path? E.g. sample first N requests and pick lowest p95 for that traffic?

maria: We tried sampling in staging and it churned decisions during bursts. Need hysteresis + sticky decisions per client route.

devon: Ops constraints: more paths => more model variants to build and test. Our CI build matrix will balloon. What's the minimal set of variants to support?

kevin: Minimal MVP: "triton-opt" and "cutlass-latency", each with compatible KV-cache serialization. For Dedicated customers we can expose both; hosted default to a routing policy.

raj: Action items then: 
- kevin: formalize routing policy heuristics (+ config schema)
- sophie: prototype runtime sampler + sticky decision state (ephemeral)
- devon: measure CI/build impact and add selective builds by route tag
- maria: add regression tests for kv-cache eviction pattern
- infra-bot: run nightly microbench sweep for seq in {16,32,64,128,512}

infra-bot: Job scheduled: nightly-kernel-sweep starting 2027-03-01 02:00UTC. Logs -> S3://redwood-qa/kernel-sweeps/nightly-1788

kevin: Also to discuss: quantized kernels. CUTLASS Q4 kernels are faster but less tolerant to mixed-precision in attention softmax. We saw output drift in rare seeds.

maria: Add eval suite check for fidelity (use existing eval prompts + perplexity + selected human evals) before enabling quant path automatically.

devon: For Dedicated, allow a flag: prefer_low_latency_kernels=true so customers can opt in. Default false for hosted unless traffic profile triggers it.

raj: Regarding fallback — if chosen path errors (OOM or unexpected kernel failure) we should auto-fallback to the other path and emit an alert. Do we have a graceful retry window?

kevin: Plan: on kernel failure, retry once with other path, track metric kernel_failover_count per-route; if > 5 in 10m -> rollback policy to safe (triton).

sophie: I've sketched a state machine for sampler + sticky decisions. Will post PR by end of week. It includes TTL for stickiness and a cooldown after failover.

maria: I'll add kv-cache eviction fuzz tests to the eval harness. Need to simulate interleaved prefix writes and partial rollbacks.

devon: CI change: add matrix build flag `KERNEL_VARIANTS=triton,cutlass` but only run both for `arch/*` smoke tests and nightly full-suite. That keeps daily cost manageable.

kevin: One more thing — we should capture per-kernel memory high-water and fragmentation metric. Suggest metric names: kernel.mem_hwm and kernel.alloc_free_jitter. Agree?

raj: yes. Also tag metrics with variant and route_id.

kevin: OK. I'll open a follow-up RFC for the routing schema + metric definitions. Sophie/maria/devon/raj please comment in the RFC.

sophie: Will do. Posting a very small prototype branch in ~2d.

maria: I'll add tests after your branch lands, @sophie.

devon: I'll scope CI changes and send PR for selective builds.

kevin: Thanks all. We'll sync in the arch sync if anything blocks. :thumbsup:
